text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- At least 31 people were killed and several other injured when flash floods, hill torrents and landslides triggered by heavy rain hit villages in Punjab and North West Frontier provinces.
- The U.S. secretary of state Madeleine Albright formally accepted an invitation to visit India later this year as a part of a trip that will also include a visit to Pakistan, her spokesman said.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif accompanied by his wife and a 70-member delegation, begins a four-day official visit to Malaysia on Thursday (July 31).

- The state's Privatisation Commission has sought permission of the government to privatise state-run Sui Northern Gas Pipeline Ltd by selling its management stake to a strategic investor rather than offloading its shares in the stock exchanges.
- The government is likely to offer the state-run Faisalabad Area Electricity Board and the Karachi Electric Supply Corporation for joint ownership to the private sector.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif would be meeting President Bill Clinton during his visit to the U.S. begining August 28.

- In a major policy shift towards Iran since the election in Tehran of a more liberal president, the Clinton administration has decided to support a $1.6 billion gas pipeline from Central Asia through Iran, in addition to one proposed through Pakistan.

- The Asian Development Bank has recommended the establishment of the National Self-Regulatory Authority or an association of brokers, dealers, and professionals for Pakistan's bourses under the supervision of the state's Corporate Law Authority to create a self-regulatory framework for the capital markets.
- The Corporate Law Authority would take severe action against those companies which have failed to provide "a reasonable return to their shareholders", sources said.
